foodie.title: Third Wave at EMA Espresso Bar
foodie.description: A bright little bar near the Powder Tower that helped start Prague's speciality coffee scene and still sets the standard for it.
foodie.bonus: Try the same bean as espresso and as filter.

foodie.title: Moravian Wine at Bokovka
foodie.description: A courtyard wine bar built around Czech and Moravian bottles nobody exports, where they will happily pour you things you cannot buy at home.
foodie.bonus: Drink a Veltínské zelené and admit it is good.

foodie.title: Chlebíčky at Sisters Bistro
foodie.description: The Czech open-faced sandwich done properly — potato salad, egg, ham, herring — at a counter that treats it as a serious format.
foodie.bonus: Order four different ones and rank them.

foodie.title: A Pint at U Zlatého Tygra
foodie.description: Bohumil Hrabal's local, where regulars have assigned seats and the beer arrives before you have finished sitting down.
foodie.bonus: Do not ask for a menu. There isn't one worth reading.

foodie.title: Goulash at Kantýna, the Butcher's Canteen
foodie.description: Order by weight at the meat counter, take a paper ticket to a shared marble table, and eat some of the best beef in the city standing up.
foodie.bonus: Get the tartare and make it yourself at the table.

foodie.title: Tank Pilsner at Lokál Dlouhá
foodie.description: Unpasteurised Pilsner Urquell poured from tanks in the cellar, in a long tiled hall doing proper Czech pub food without the tourist markup.
foodie.bonus: Order a šnyt or a mlíko and find out what you actually got.

foodie.title: Coffee at Kavárna Slavia
foodie.description: The riverside café opposite the National Theatre where dissidents, actors and Havel all sat, still serving cake under the same green lamps.
foodie.bonus: Get a window table facing the castle.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Field
foodie.description: A Michelin-starred room a block from the Old Town doing Czech ingredients with real wit — dishes arrive looking like the field they came out of.
foodie.bonus: Take the full pairing rather than the short one.

foodie.title: St. Norbert in the Strahov Monastery Courtyard
foodie.description: Drink amber, dark and IPA lagers brewed on the monastery grounds, in a courtyard a hundred metres from the Strahov library halls.
foodie.bonus: Ask the brewer which beer they'd pick for themselves

foodie.title: Trdelník Straight Off the Coals at Good Food
foodie.description: Watch the dough spiral-roast over open coals on Karlova, then eat Prague's cinnamon-sugar chimney cake while it is still too hot to hold.
foodie.bonus: Get the ice cream-filled version instead of plain

foodie.title: The Set Menu at Benjamin in Vinohrady
foodie.description: A small neighbourhood room off Mánesova doing a multi-course Czech set menu that locals book out long before the guidebook crowd finds it.
foodie.bonus: Let the server pick your wine pairing

foodie.title: Svíčková at U Fleků, Brewing Since 1499
foodie.description: Sit at a long communal table in a five-century-old beer hall and work through Czech classics with the house dark lager.
foodie.bonus: Order in Czech, even if you have to read it off your phone

chill.title: Letná Beer Garden Above the River
chill.description: Plastic cups, long trestle tables and a view straight down the line of Vltava bridges from the top of Letná park.
chill.bonus: Stay from daylight through to the bridges lighting up.

chill.title: Sunset from Riegrovy Sady
chill.description: The sloping lawn in Vinohrady where the whole neighbourhood brings a bottle and sits facing the castle as the light goes.
chill.bonus: Bring the bottle. Sit on the slope, not the benches.

chill.title: Read Inside the Book Tower
chill.description: The Municipal Library's Idiom sculpture is a column of books with a mirror inside, making an infinite shaft of spines — then stay and read in the library itself.
chill.bonus: Put your head fully inside and look up.

chill.title: Kampa Island and the Lennon Wall
chill.description: Drop off Charles Bridge onto the quiet island below it, follow the mill stream, and end at a wall that has been repainted continuously since 1980.
chill.bonus: Add something to the wall. It is expected.

chill.title: Peacocks in the Wallenstein Garden
chill.description: The Senate's baroque garden below the castle, with a dripstone grotto wall, a carp pond and white peacocks that wander up to you.
chill.bonus: Find the faces hidden in the grotto wall.

chill.title: The Terraces of Vrtba Garden
chill.description: A small baroque garden climbing the hillside in Malá Strana in stone terraces, almost always empty despite being minutes from the crowds.
chill.bonus: Go to the very top terrace and stay there a while.

chill.title: Coffee and Boat-Watching on the Náplavka
chill.description: Take a coffee out to the deckchairs on the Rašínovo nábřeží embankment and give the Vltava traffic an hour of your attention and nothing else.
chill.bonus: Stay for a second coffee you didn't plan on

chill.title: Wander the Walled Paths of Vyšehrad Cemetery
chill.description: Walk quiet gravel paths past the graves of Czech composers and artists, with the Vltava spread out below the fortress walls.
chill.bonus: Find the grave of a composer whose music you already know

chill.title: Sit Inside the Klementinum's Baroque Library Hall
chill.description: Join a small guided visit into one of the world's most beautiful libraries, its frescoed ceiling glowing over centuries-old books.
chill.bonus: Pick the one shelf you'd want to read cover to cover

chill.title: Cross Charles Bridge at Sunrise, Before the Crowds
chill.description: Walk the 600-year-old bridge in the quiet gray light, just you, the baroque statues, and a handful of early risers.
chill.bonus: Touch the same statue tourists always crowd around later

adventure.title: Divoká Šárka's Wild Valley
adventure.description: A rocky gorge inside the city limits with cliffs, woodland trails and an open-air swimming reservoir at the bottom of it.
adventure.bonus: Swim in the reservoir, however cold it is.

adventure.title: Climb Vítkov Hill to the Iron Horseman
adventure.description: A steep walk up out of Žižkov to one of the largest equestrian statues on earth, with the best free panorama of the city behind it.
adventure.bonus: Get there for sunset and stay for the lights.

adventure.title: Bohemian Switzerland and the Pravčická Brána
adventure.description: A full day north to the largest natural sandstone arch in Europe, plus a punt ride through the Kamenice gorge between vertical rock walls.
adventure.bonus: Do the gorge boats as well as the arch — most people skip them.

adventure.title: Up the Žižkov Television Tower
adventure.description: Ride to the observation deck of the communist-era rocket the city loves to hate, with David Černý's faceless babies crawling up the outside.
adventure.bonus: Find the glass floor panel and stand on it.

adventure.title: Whitewater at the Troja Channel
adventure.description: Prague's artificial slalom course, where the Olympic team trains and where you can book a raft through the same rapids.
adventure.bonus: Go through the biggest drop without bracing.

adventure.title: Cycle the Vltava Trail South
adventure.description: Pick up the A2 riverside cycle path and ride out of the centre until the tour boats give way to weirs, herons and beer gardens.
adventure.bonus: Stop at the first riverside pub you pass and turn back after it.

adventure.title: Climb the Limestone at Prokopské údolí
adventure.description: A protected karst valley on the edge of Prague where Devonian limestone crags rise straight out of the woods and locals climb after work.
adventure.bonus: Walk the valley floor first and pick your route from below.

adventure.title: 287 Steps Up St. Vitus Cathedral
adventure.description: A tight spiral staircase inside the Great South Tower, ending at a gallery where the whole castle district drops away beneath you.
adventure.bonus: Count the steps yourself and see if you agree.

adventure.title: Explore the Underground Vyšehrad Casemates
adventure.description: Duck into the brick tunnels beneath Vyšehrad fortress and stand face to face with the original Charles Bridge statues stored in the Gorlice hall.
adventure.bonus: Guess which statue is the original before reading the sign

adventure.title: Pedal a Boat Under Prague Castle from Slovanka
adventure.description: Take a pedal boat off the Slovanka jetty on Slovanský ostrov and push out into the Vltava for a low, unobstructed line on the castle and Charles Bridge.
adventure.bonus: Paddle all the way to the base of Charles Bridge and back

adventure.title: Hike the Old Castle Stairs Up to Prague Castle
adventure.description: Skip the tram and climb the steep, centuries-old stone stairway from Malá Strana straight up to the castle gates.
adventure.bonus: Don't stop to rest until you reach the top

adventure.title: Run the Riverside Path Through Stromovka Park
adventure.description: Get a sunrise run in through Prague's largest park, looping past ponds, old oaks, and the Výstaviště exhibition grounds.
adventure.bonus: Run past the Výstaviště fountain without checking your phone

adventure.title: Climb the Old Town Bridge Tower for a Charles Bridge View
adventure.description: Climb the narrow spiral stairs of the Gothic tower guarding Charles Bridge for one of the best rooftop views of the river.
adventure.bonus: Count how many bridge towers you can spot from the top

adventure.title: Day Trip to Karlštejn Castle
adventure.description: Take the short train out of the city to climb through a 14th-century royal castle perched on a forested hilltop above the Berounka valley.
adventure.bonus: Walk the whole hill road up to the castle instead of the shuttle

adventure.title: A Beer Bath at Bernard Beer Spa
adventure.description: Sink into a larch-wood tub of warm water, hops and malt with your own Bernard tap at arm's reach, then sweat the rest of it out in the relaxation room.
adventure.bonus: Finish the pint that's included before you get out

adventure.title: Climb the Petřín Lookout Tower After the Funicular Ride Up
adventure.description: Ride the century-old funicular up Petřín Hill, then climb the mini Eiffel Tower for a rooftop view over Prague's spires.
adventure.bonus: Take the stairs instead of the elevator at the top

social.title: Sparta Praha Ice Hockey Night
social.description: Czech league hockey at full volume — organised chanting, a drum section, and beer sold by the metre in the concourse.
social.bonus: Learn one chant and join in by the second period.

social.title: A Night Inside Cross Club
social.description: A Holešovice club built entirely out of welded scrap that moves, lights up and rotates around you, with a garden and three floors of music.
social.bonus: Explore every floor before you settle on one.

social.title: Signal Festival Lights Up the City
social.description: For four October nights the whole centre becomes a light-art trail, with projections thrown across baroque facades and half the city walking it together.
social.bonus: Do the full route on foot rather than picking two stops.

social.title: Late at Roxy
social.description: A stripped-back former cinema in the Old Town that has been booking serious electronic line-ups since the early nineties.
social.bonus: Arrive after 1am, which is when it actually starts.

social.title: Cocktails at Hemingway Bar
social.description: A small, dark, absinthe-heavy bar near the river that put Prague on the world cocktail map and still takes it extremely seriously.
social.bonus: Let them make you something off-menu.

social.title: Find the Door at Anonymous Bar
social.description: A Guy Fawkes-masked speakeasy off Michalská where the drinks come out on fire, in smoke boxes, or in something that is not a glass.
social.bonus: Order the one the bartender warns you about.

social.title: Parukářka Hill with a Bottle
social.description: Žižkov's scruffy hilltop park with a beer hut, a skate bowl and the best low-effort city view in Prague.
social.bonus: Talk to whoever is sitting on the next bench.

social.title: Jazz in the Cellar at Reduta
social.description: Prague's oldest jazz club, a low vaulted room on Národní where Bill Clinton once got handed a saxophone and played.
social.bonus: Book the front table — the room is small enough that it matters.

social.title: Shop the Saturday Náplavka Farmers Market
social.description: Browse stalls of Czech cheese, bread, and produce alongside locals doing their weekend shop along the river.
social.bonus: Buy a snack from a vendor with no English menu

social.title: Monday Pub Quiz at the Czech Inn
social.description: Turn up alone, get folded into a team of strangers, and spend a Monday night arguing over trivia in the basement bar of a Vršovice hostel.
social.bonus: Join a team you don't already know

social.title: A Small-Room Set at Palác Akropolis
social.description: Žižkov's old theatre turned music house, where the line-up swings from indie to Saharan desert blues and the crowd is close enough to touch the stage.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the group next to you

social.title: Drinks on the Náplavka as the Sun Goes Down
social.description: Join the after-work crowd spilling along the Rašínovo nábřeží embankment and its moored boats for beers facing the water.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with someone at the next boat over

culture.title: The Apostles on the Astronomical Clock
culture.description: Watch the 1410 orloj do its hourly parade of apostles and a skeleton ringing a bell, then go up the Old Town Hall tower it is bolted to.
culture.bonus: Take the lift up but walk the ramp down.

culture.title: The Old Jewish Cemetery and the Spanish Synagogue
culture.description: Twelve thousand headstones stacked over each other because the quarter was never allowed to expand, and a Moorish-revival synagogue gilded floor to ceiling.
culture.bonus: Read the names painted in the Pinkas Synagogue before you leave.

culture.title: Kutná Hora and the Bone Church
culture.description: An hour east by train: a silver-mining town with a cathedral built by miners, and an ossuary decorated with the bones of forty thousand people.
culture.bonus: Do St. Barbara's as well — most day-trippers only do the bones.

culture.title: Mozart at the Estates Theatre
culture.description: Don Giovanni premiered in this pale green horseshoe of a theatre in 1787, with Mozart conducting, and it is still staged in the same room.
culture.bonus: Sit in the boxes rather than the stalls.

culture.title: Museum Kampa and the Crawling Babies
culture.description: Central European modern art in a converted riverside mill, with three of David Černý's giant faceless infants on the lawn outside.
culture.bonus: Find the Kupka room and give it ten full minutes.

culture.title: The Strahov Library Halls
culture.description: Two baroque halls — Theological and Philosophical — with frescoed ceilings, globes and a cabinet of curiosities including a preserved narwhal tusk.
culture.bonus: Look for the shark and the dodo remains in the corridor.

culture.title: Modern Art in the Veletržní Palác
culture.description: A vast functionalist trade-fair building holding the National Gallery's modern collection — Czech cubism, plus a Picasso and a Klimt or two.
culture.bonus: Take the top floor first and work down.

culture.title: The Czech Philharmonic at the Rudolfinum
culture.description: Dvořák conducted the orchestra's first concert in this hall in 1896, and hearing his own music played in it remains the single best night in Prague.
culture.bonus: Go to a programme with Dvořák or Smetana on it.

8ball.title: Order the Thing You Cannot Pronounce
8ball.description: Walk into any Czech pub without an English menu, point at the longest word on the board, and eat whatever arrives.
8ball.bonus: No translating it until after the first bite.

8ball.title: Ride Tram 22 to the End of the Line
8ball.description: Take the city's best tram route past the castle and keep going well past where you were supposed to get off, then walk back toward the river.
8ball.bonus: Get a beer at the first pub you see after you get off.
